subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class browser-plugin config for per-profile proxies plus per-agent/subagent browser-profile binding, and what proxy-secret, SSRF, and session-ownership contract should that use?
rationale: The missing capability is source-confirmed, but implementing it defines public config, browser egress policy, proxy credential handling, and agent/session ownership semantics that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Approve core browser contract
options.body: Design and approve a browser-plugin contract for proxy secrets, per-agent inheritance, concurrency limits, tab ownership, and diagnostics before implementation.

options.title: Split remaining work
options.body: Keep this umbrella open while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/60035 owns general proxy policy and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/85672 owns subagent attachment and operator visibility semantics.

options.title: Defer to external orchestration
options.body: Document remote CDP, multiple Gateways, browser-lock-style wrappers, or ClawHub packages as the supported path and close only after maintainers decide not to add core config.

recommendation.title: Approve core browser contract
recommendation.body: Design and approve a browser-plugin contract for proxy secrets, per-agent inheritance, concurrency limits, tab ownership, and diagnostics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across browser profile config, browser plugin ownership, docs, and security-sensitive browser control paths.
